sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you live or work in a city, sitting in traffic is probably a big part of your life.
sentences.zh: 如果你在城市里生活或工作，堵车大概是你生活中很大的一部分。

sentences.en: The Lincoln, about 20 to 30 out.
sentences.zh: 林肯隧道，大约还要20到30分钟。

sentences.en: And the inbound side, we had about a 20-minute delay.
sentences.zh: 进城方向，我们遇到了大约20分钟的延误。

sentences.en: Here in Washington, D.C., we take perverse pride in having some of the worst traffic in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿特区，我们对拥有全美最糟糕的交通状况感到一种变态的自豪。

sentences.en: But on a global scale, D.C.
sentences.zh: 但放眼全球，华盛顿特区

sentences.en: has nothing on London or Istanbul, Rio or Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 根本比不上伦敦、伊斯坦布尔、里约热内卢或墨西哥城。

sentences.en: On today's episode, we're going to explore all kinds of interventions that can make traffic better.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将探讨各种能够改善交通状况的干预措施。

sentences.en: We're also going to look at the interventions that are supposed to make traffic better, but don't.
sentences.zh: 我们还将审视那些本应改善交通却适得其反的干预措施。

sentences.en: I feel like we should put together the International Journal of Unintended Consequences and send them to lawmakers all over the planet.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们应该汇编一本《国际意外后果期刊》，然后寄给全世界的立法者们。

sentences.en: Before we get there, we want to take you on a quick trip around some of the world's most congested cities.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，我们想带你快速游览一下世界上一些最拥堵的城市。

sentences.en: Producer Maggie Penman reached out to NPR correspondents stationed in Asia, Africa and Europe.
sentences.zh: 制片人玛吉·彭曼联系了驻扎在亚洲、非洲和欧洲的NPR记者。

sentences.en: She's also going to tell us about a little traffic culture clash of her own.
sentences.zh: 她还要告诉我们她自己经历的一场小小的交通文化冲突。

sentences.en: So a few years ago, I'm out in L.A.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我在洛杉矶

sentences.en: for a couple of days for work.
sentences.zh: 出差待了几天。

sentences.en: I'm driving a rented car.
sentences.zh: 我开着一辆租来的车。

sentences.en: And I come up to a busy intersection.
sentences.zh: 我来到一个繁忙的十字路口。

sentences.en: And I'm trying to turn left.
sentences.zh: 我想左转。

sentences.en: I have my blinker on.
sentences.zh: 我打着转向灯。

sentences.en: I'm in the left-hand turn lane.
sentences.zh: 我停在左转车道上。

sentences.en: And the light is green.
sentences.zh: 绿灯亮着。

sentences.en: But there are still tons of cars coming through the intersection.
sentences.zh: 但十字路口依然有源源不断的车流。

sentences.en: So I patiently sit there, waiting my turn.
sentences.zh: 所以我耐心地坐在那儿，等待轮到我通行。

sentences.en: And the light turns yellow.
sentences.zh: 接着黄灯亮了。

sentences.en: And there are still cars coming through the intersection.
sentences.zh: 十字路口还是有车在通过。

sentences.en: And then the light turns red.
sentences.zh: 然后红灯亮了。

sentences.en: I think, okay, I'll just wait until the light turns green again.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我就等到绿灯再亮吧。

sentences.en: Big mistake.
sentences.zh: 大错特错。

sentences.en: The cars behind me start honking like crazy.
sentences.zh: 我后面的车开始疯狂按喇叭。

sentences.en: I can see the guy in my rearview mirror.
sentences.zh: 我能从后视镜里看到那个人。

sentences.en: And he's losing it.
sentences.zh: 他快崩溃了。

sentences.en: Yelling, hitting his steering wheel in frustration.
sentences.zh: 大喊大叫，沮丧地拍打着方向盘。

sentences.en: When the light does turn green again, I'm now determined to make this left turn.
sentences.zh: 当绿灯再次亮起时，我下定决心一定要完成这次左转。

sentences.en: And the guy behind me turns too.
sentences.zh: 我后面的那个人也转了过来。

sentences.en: And then passes me immediately.
sentences.zh: 然后立刻超过了我。

sentences.en: Yelling out his window and flipping me off.
sentences.zh: 对着窗外大喊大叫，还对我竖中指。

sentences.en: At the next intersection, the woman who was behind him pulls up next to me and signals
sentences.zh: 在下一个路口，那个在他后面的女人把车停在我旁边，示意

sentences.en: for me to roll my window down.
sentences.zh: 我摇下车窗。

sentences.en: And she's this kind-looking lady, probably about my mother's age.
sentences.zh: 她看起来很和善，大概和我母亲年纪差不多。

sentences.en: And I thought she was going to commiserate with me about how crazy that guy was.
sentences.zh: 我以为她是想跟我一起吐槽那个男人有多疯狂。

sentences.en: But no, then she starts yelling at me too.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，她也开始对我大吼大叫。

sentences.en: Why didn't you go?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不走？

sentences.en: Were you texting?
sentences.zh: 你在发短信吗？

sentences.en: What's wrong with you?
sentences.zh: 你有毛病吗？

sentences.en: So I get to the NPR West office.
sentences.zh: 于是我到了NPR西部办公室。

sentences.en: And I'm very shaken up.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And I describe this experience to a couple of my colleagues who live and work in L.A.
sentences.zh: 我向几位在洛杉矶生活和工作的同事描述了这段经历。

sentences.en: And they're both like, oh yeah, you probably should have gone.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，哦，是的，你当时可能应该直接开过去。

sentences.en: So we confirmed for you that you are indeed crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们向你证实，你确实是个怪胎。

sentences.en: At least in L.A.
sentences.zh: 至少在洛杉矶

sentences.en: you are.
sentences.zh: 你是。

sentences.en: That's Arzu Rezvani, an editor at Morning Edition, who works out of NPR's L.A.
sentences.zh: 那是阿尔祖·雷兹瓦尼，《早间新闻》的一位编辑，她在NPR洛杉矶

sentences.en: Bureau.
sentences.zh: 分社工作。

sentences.en: She was one of the people I was meeting that day.
sentences.zh: 她就是那天我见到的其中一个人。

sentences.en: And I recently called her up to try and get some insight about why my style of driving
sentences.zh: 最近我给她打了电话，想了解一下为什么我的驾驶风格

sentences.en: was so frustrating to L.A.
sentences.zh: 会让洛杉矶的

sentences.en: drivers.
sentences.zh: 司机们如此沮丧。

sentences.en: You have to kind of float in the middle of an intersection when you want to make a left
sentences.zh: 当你想要左转

sentences.en: or right turn.
sentences.zh: 或右转时，你得悬停在十字路口中间。

sentences.en: You got to wait for the car's oncoming traffic to, you know, finish up.
sentences.zh: 你得等对向车流，你知道的，走完。

sentences.en: And sometimes that means making that turn on a red.
sentences.zh: 有时这意味着要在红灯时完成转弯。

sentences.en: So wait, I was supposed to run the red light?
sentences.zh: 等等，我是说我应该闯红灯吗？

sentences.en: By the book, that's illegal, right?
sentences.zh: 按规定，那是违法的，对吧？

sentences.en: But there's just a new normal that is introduced in cities like Los Angeles.
sentences.zh: 但在像洛杉矶这样的城市，出现了一种新的常态。

sentences.en: And you just kind of got to go with the flow.
sentences.zh: 你只能随波逐流。

sentences.en: I was really curious about this new normal that Arzu was talking about.
sentences.zh: 我对阿尔祖所说的这种新常态感到非常好奇。

sentences.en: And I wondered whether other cities had unspoken rules or conventions, too.
sentences.zh: 我想知道其他城市是否也有不成文的规则或惯例。

sentences.en: When you come to a light and it turns green, the automatic thing to do if you want to take
sentences.zh: 当你来到红绿灯路口，绿灯亮起时，如果你想

sentences.en: a left turn is to immediately rush and take a left across three or four lanes of traffic.
sentences.zh: 左转，自动的做法就是立刻冲过去，横穿三四条车道完成左转。

sentences.en: The first person I thought to ask was Frank Langfitt, who, in addition to being NPR's
sentences.zh: 我第一个想到要问的人是弗兰克·朗菲特，他除了担任NPR

sentences.en: correspondent based in Shanghai, has also occasionally driven a taxi around the city to find stories.
sentences.zh: 驻上海记者外，偶尔还会开出租车穿梭于城市中寻找故事。

sentences.en: It's like being in a game where anything can come at you at any time from any angle.
sentences.zh: 这就像在玩一个游戏，任何东西都可能随时从任何角度向你袭来。

sentences.en: So a stop sign, a light is not entirely relevant, but not very relevant.
sentences.zh: 所以停车标志、红绿灯并不是完全相关，或者说没那么重要。

sentences.en: So when I go through intersections, I look right, I look left, I look right again.
sentences.zh: 所以当我通过十字路口时，我会看右边，看左边，再看右边。

sentences.en: The norm in Shanghai is that traffic laws are more like suggestions.
sentences.zh: 在上海，交通法规更像是建议。

sentences.en: Here in Shanghai, there's not a lot of enforcement.
sentences.zh: 在上海，执法力度并不大。

sentences.en: And I'm amazed when I get a ticket.
sentences.zh: 所以我收到罚单时都很惊讶。

sentences.en: I was pulled over a while ago for being in the wrong turn lane, which was just kind of
sentences.zh: 前阵子我因为走错转弯车道被拦下，考虑到警察允许人们在这里做的所有事情，

sentences.en: comical considering all the things that the cops allow people to do here.
sentences.zh: 这简直有点滑稽。

sentences.en: But considering all of this, I was shocked when Frank told me about another norm.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到这一切，当弗兰克告诉我另一个准则时，我震惊了。

sentences.en: There's almost no road rage.
sentences.zh: 这里几乎没有路怒症。

sentences.en: As long as the cars never touch, people just let it go.
sentences.zh: 只要车子没碰到，人们就随它去了。

sentences.en: And I think it's, maybe it's partly a function.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能部分是一个功能。

sentences.en: I don't understand all of this, even though I've been here a long time.
sentences.zh: 我并不完全理解这一切，尽管我在这里待了很久。

sentences.en: It may be a function if this is such a crowded country, especially these big cities on the
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个功能，因为这是一个如此拥挤的国家，尤其是这些东海岸的大城市，

sentences.en: East Coast, that if you were going to get angry about this stuff, you'd just have a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 如果你要为这些事情生气，你早就心脏病发作了。

sentences.en: In fact, he said.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他说。

sentences.en: I'm the only one who has road rage.
sentences.zh: 我是唯一一个有路怒症的人。

sentences.en: I'm like the only guy in the city who has road rage.
sentences.zh: 我简直是这个城市里唯一一个有路怒症的人。

sentences.en: I also talked to NPR's correspondent in Nairobi, Greg Warner, and he told me Nairobi is one
sentences.zh: 我还和NPR驻内罗毕记者格雷格·华纳谈过，他告诉我内罗毕是他住过的

sentences.en: of the most polite cities he's ever lived in.
sentences.zh: 最礼貌的城市之一。

sentences.en: For instance, nobody cuts in line.
sentences.zh: 例如，没人会插队。

sentences.en: But when it comes to driving, Greg says, all that changes.
sentences.zh: 但说到开车，格雷格说，一切都变了。

sentences.en: One of the main features of driving in Nairobi, according to Greg, is that there are very
sentences.zh: 据格雷格说，在内罗毕开车的一个主要特点是，几乎

sentences.en: few traffic lights.
sentences.zh: 没有交通信号灯。

sentences.en: There are occasionally like a random traffic light you'll see, but nobody actually pays
sentences.zh: 偶尔你会看到一个随机的交通灯，但实际上没人会

sentences.en: attention to it.
sentences.zh: 理会它。

sentences.en: It has no actual meaning.
sentences.zh: 它没有任何实际意义。

sentences.en: It just turns green and red and for no particular reason.
sentences.zh: 它只是毫无理由地变绿又变红。

sentences.en: So how do people know when to go?
sentences.zh: 那么人们怎么知道什么时候该走呢？

sentences.en: It's all convention.
sentences.zh: 全靠惯例。

sentences.en: And so in this situation, what I would think people would do is a kind of honor system like,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我认为人们会采取一种荣誉制度，比如：

sentences.en: okay, yeah, you went.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你走了。

sentences.en: Okay, now let me go.
sentences.zh: 好，现在轮到我了。

sentences.en: That lane hasn't gone for a while.
sentences.zh: 那条车道已经很久没动了。

sentences.en: Like just a kind of understanding, but it's actually just a complete free for all.
sentences.zh: 就像是一种默契，但实际上完全是一场混战。

sentences.en: Everybody's trying to go at once.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想同时通过。

sentences.en: And every four-lane intersection is like a gridlock.
sentences.zh: 每一个四车道十字路口都像是一团乱麻。

sentences.en: And it's not just a gridlock where, you know, some cars will kind of inch forward, but it's
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是交通堵塞，你知道的，有些车会慢慢向前挪动，而是

sentences.en: like a twisted knot where I'm behind your bumper and they're behind their bumper.
sentences.zh: 像一个扭曲的结，我被困在你的保险杠后面，他们被困在别人的保险杠后面。

sentences.en: And it's like this interlocked, you know, kind of origami or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就像这种交织在一起的，你知道的，某种折纸艺术之类的东西。

sentences.en: I also talked to Rich Preston, NPR's producer in London.
sentences.zh: 我还和NPR驻伦敦制片人里奇·普雷斯顿谈过。

sentences.en: And the primary feature of driving in the UK is, of course, that you drive on the left.
sentences.zh: 在英国开车的主要特点当然是靠左行驶。

sentences.en: And as the London producer dealing with visiting American correspondents, I see this a lot,
sentences.zh: 作为一名负责接待来访美国记者的伦敦制片人，我经常看到这种情况，

sentences.en: is visitors to the United Kingdom stepping out into the road, not looking down the road
sentences.zh: 就是来英国的游客走上马路时，没有往

sentences.en: the right way.
sentences.zh: 正确的方向看路。

sentences.en: Rich travels around for work and is pretty accustomed to switching sides and driving on
sentences.zh: 里奇经常因工作出差，已经很习惯切换方向并在

sentences.en: the right.
sentences.zh: 右侧行驶。

sentences.en: But occasionally, that rule of thumb gets him into trouble.
sentences.zh: 但偶尔，那条经验法则也会让他陷入麻烦。

sentences.en: There's that mentality of, oh, I'm in another country.
sentences.zh: 有一种心态是，哦，我在另一个国家。

sentences.en: I'm going to have to drive on the right-hand side that I started driving on the right-hand
sentences.zh: 我得在右侧行驶，我开始在爱尔兰的道路右侧

sentences.en: side of the road in Ireland, even though I should have been sticking on the left.
sentences.zh: 开车，尽管我本应该坚持靠左行驶。

sentences.en: And even when he's back home in London, Rich says driving can be pretty scary.
sentences.zh: 即使回到伦敦的家中，里奇也说开车可能相当可怕。

sentences.en: Because the thing about London is it's such an old city, it's really hard to make more
sentences.zh: 因为伦敦的问题在于它是一座如此古老的城市，很难为

sentences.en: space for all the people that are here.
sentences.zh: 这里的所有人腾出更多空间。

sentences.en: Rich mostly cycles around the city these days, but he can still be found honking at drivers.
sentences.zh: 里奇现在大部分时间骑自行车在城里穿梭，但他仍然会被发现对着司机按喇叭。

sentences.en: I actually bought a horn for my bike, which is this small thing that clips onto the handlebars
sentences.zh: 我其实给我的自行车买了一个喇叭，这是一个夹在车把上的小东西，

sentences.en: and it's an kind of electronic horn and it's about 140 decibels.
sentences.zh: 是一种电子喇叭，大约有140分贝。

sentences.en: And it saved my life on so many occasions, I can guarantee it.
sentences.zh: 我可以保证，它在很多场合都救了我的命。

sentences.en: I asked Rich to collect some sound of his commute home yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我让里奇收集了一些他昨天回家路上的声音。

sentences.en: So I'm going to leave you on this somewhat shrill note.
sentences.zh: 所以我要以这个略显刺耳的声音结束。

sentences.en: All right, I hope you made it home safely.
sentences.zh: 好了，希望你平安到家。

sentences.en: That's Hidden Brain producer Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 那是《Hidden Brain》的制片人玛吉·彭曼。

sentences.en: After a short break, Dan Pink is going to be back on the show to play a round of Stopwatch
sentences.zh: 短暂休息后，丹·平克将回到节目中与我进行一轮“秒表科学”

sentences.en: Science with me.
sentences.zh: 环节。

sentences.en: We're going to tell you about interesting social science research on what works and doesn't
sentences.zh: 我们将告诉你关于解决交通拥堵什么有效、什么无效的有趣的社会科学研究。

sentences.en: work to fix traffic congestion.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，即使控制了人口增长因素，修建额外的道路也导致了

sentences.en: They found, even controlling for population growth, that constructing additional roads led
sentences.zh: 更多的交通拥堵，而不是更少。

sentences.en: to more traffic congestion, not less.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 现在回到“秒表科学”的另一轮环节。

sentences.en: Back now for another round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 和我在一起的依然是我们的资深“秒表科学”记者丹尼尔·平克。

sentences.en: I'm joined as always by Daniel Pink, our senior Stopwatch Science correspondent.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，丹。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dan.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Thank you, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 在“秒表科学”中，丹和我每人有60秒的时间来总结有趣的社会科学

sentences.en: On Stopwatch Science, Dan and I give one another 60 seconds to summarize interesting social science
sentences.zh: 研究。

sentences.en: research.
sentences.zh: 当我们接近60秒大关时，我们的制片人会用音乐淹没我们的声音，就像他们在

sentences.en: As we approach the 60-second mark, our producers will drown us out with music, just like they
sentences.zh: 奥斯卡颁奖典礼上做的那样。

sentences.en: do at the Oscars.
sentences.zh: （注：此条为补充编号，对应原输入最后一条）

sentences.en: Our topic today is traffic.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的话题是交通。

sentences.en: You hate it, you deal with it, maybe you are even in it right now.
sentences.zh: 你讨厌它，你得应付它，甚至你现在可能就身处其中。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to explore what works and what doesn't work in easing congestion and
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨在缓解拥堵和

sentences.en: improving traffic safety.
sentences.zh: 改善交通安全方面，哪些方法有效，哪些无效。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're ready, your first 60 seconds starts now.
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你准备好了，你的第一个60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Well, there's one easy, if expensive solution, and that's just to build more roads, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个简单但昂贵的解决方案，那就是多修路，对吧？

sentences.en: Makes sense.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: Well, maybe not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许并非如此。

sentences.en: Two economists writing in the American Economic Review analyzed two decades' worth of data
sentences.zh: 两位在《美国经济评论》上发表文章的经济学家分析了二十年的数据，

sentences.en: on U.S.
sentences.zh: 关于美国

sentences.en: commuting times and road construction.
sentences.zh: 通勤时间和道路建设的数据。

sentences.en: They found, even controlling for population growth, that constructing additional roads led to more
sentences.zh: 他们发现，即使控制了人口增长因素，修建更多的道路反而导致了

sentences.en: traffic congestion, not less.
sentences.zh: 更多的交通拥堵，而不是更少。

sentences.en: Now, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是怎么回事呢？

sentences.en: Even though this paper is a complex bear of statistical analysis, the core explanation is
sentences.zh: 尽管这篇论文是一份复杂的统计分析报告，但其核心解释

sentences.en: simple.
sentences.zh: 很简单。

sentences.en: Supply and demand.
sentences.zh: 供需关系。

sentences.en: When we build roads, we increase the supply of driving opportunities.
sentences.zh: 当我们修建道路时，我们增加了驾驶机会的供给。

sentences.en: Increasing the supply of something generally reduces its price.
sentences.zh: 增加某样东西的供给通常会降低其价格。

sentences.en: But driving, it turns out, is extremely responsive to price changes.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，驾驶对价格变化极其敏感。

sentences.en: The lower price, that is, more room on the roads, increases demand again.
sentences.zh: 价格降低，也就是道路上有了更多空间，这再次增加了需求。

sentences.en: More individuals and commercial truckers now want to drive, and they recongest the roads.
sentences.zh: 现在更多的个人和商业卡车司机想要开车，他们又让道路重新拥堵起来。

sentences.en: Economists call it the fundamental law of highway congestion.
sentences.zh: 经济学家称之为公路拥堵的基本定律。

sentences.en: More roads cause more traffic.
sentences.zh: 更多的道路导致更多的交通。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, policymakers ignore the law, and the result is futility.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，政策制定者忽视了这条定律，结果就是徒劳无功。

sentences.en: So I'm guessing the solution to this is more public transit.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜解决办法是增加公共交通。

sentences.en: You would think.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么想。

sentences.en: But what the research also shows is that adding public transportation also increases congestion
sentences.zh: 但研究也表明，增加公共交通也会增加拥堵，

sentences.en: for the exact same reason.
sentences.zh: 原因完全相同。

sentences.en: It lowers the price of driving.
sentences.zh: 它降低了驾驶的成本。

sentences.en: Driving responds to price changes.
sentences.zh: 驾驶对价格变化有反应。

sentences.en: More people then get on the roads.
sentences.zh: 于是更多的人上了路。

sentences.en: So more public transit doesn't help.
sentences.zh: 所以增加公共交通没用。

sentences.en: More roads don't help.
sentences.zh: 修更多的路也没用。

sentences.en: We just have to resign ourselves to traffic jaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们只能听天由命，忍受交通堵塞。

sentences.en: Well, what we have to do is, I think, we have to start thinking like economists and
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们必须做的是，开始像经济学家一样思考，

sentences.en: realize how much driving depends on price.
sentences.zh: 意识到驾驶在多大程度上取决于价格。

sentences.en: And so the best thing to do is something that is deeply politically unpopular, which is to
sentences.zh: 所以最好的做法是采取一些在政治上极不受欢迎的措施，那就是

sentences.en: raise the price of driving, perhaps through congestion chargers or higher tolls.
sentences.zh: 提高驾驶成本，或许可以通过拥堵费或更高的过路费来实现。

sentences.en: I think Dan Ping just declared the president, and I suspect he's not going to win.
sentences.zh: 我觉得丹·平刚才宣布要竞选总统了，但我怀疑他赢不了。

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: But maybe you can win, Shankar, on your next 60 seconds, which begins right now.
sentences.zh: 但也许你能赢，尚卡尔，在你的下一个60秒里，现在开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: When you enact laws or make policies that affect human beings, it's often easy to forget that
sentences.zh: 当你制定影响人类的法律或政策时，往往容易忘记

sentences.en: you're dealing with a dynamic system, which is exactly what you were just talking about,
sentences.zh: 你正在处理一个动态系统，这正是你刚才所说的，

sentences.en: Dan.
sentences.zh: 丹。

sentences.en: People adapt to new rules, often in ways that policymakers don't anticipate.
sentences.zh: 人们会适应新规则，方式往往是政策制定者预料不到的。

sentences.en: In the late 1980s, Mexico City was dealing with a pollution problem.
sentences.zh: 20世纪80年代末，墨西哥城正在处理污染问题。

sentences.en: Lawmakers said, let's pass a new law.
sentences.zh: 立法者说，让我们通过一项新法律。

sentences.en: They banned drivers from the road one day each week.
sentences.zh: 他们禁止司机每周有一天开车上路。

sentences.en: The day you were not allowed to drive was calculated based on the last digits of your car license
sentences.zh: 禁止你开车的那一天是根据你车牌号码的最后一位数字

sentences.en: plate number.
sentences.zh: 计算出来的。

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: One simple law, 20% fewer cars on the road each day.
sentences.zh: 一条简单的法律，每天路上的车少了20%。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: What could go wrong?
sentences.zh: 能出什么问题呢？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Lucas Davis at the University of Michigan finds that pollution did not decline as a result of
sentences.zh: 密歇根大学的卢卡斯·戴维斯发现，墨西哥城的污染并没有因为

sentences.en: the measure in Mexico City.
sentences.zh: 这项措施而减少。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Drivers went out and bought more cars.
sentences.zh: 司机们跑去买了更多的车。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: If I can't drive my Toyota on Mondays, I'm going to drive my Chevy instead.
sentences.zh: 如果我周一不能开我的丰田，那我就开我的雪佛兰。

sentences.en: Even worse, the law triggered an increase in older, more polluting cars, perhaps because
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，这项法律导致了更老旧、污染更严重的汽车增加，可能是因为

sentences.en: buying a new car is expensive.
sentences.zh: 买新车很贵。

sentences.en: So drivers bought an old gas-guzzling clunker to drive the one day of the week they could
sentences.zh: 所以司机们买了一辆耗油的老破车，在他们不能使用常规车辆的那一天

sentences.en: not use their regular car.
sentences.zh: 开这辆车。

sentences.en: I feel that lawmakers around the world should be asked to sign the Hippocratic oath, Dan,
sentences.zh: 我觉得全世界的立法者都应该被要求签署希波克拉底誓言，丹，

sentences.en: first, do no car.
sentences.zh: 首先，不要造成伤害（不要造成车害）。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I feel like we should put together the International Journal of Unintended Consequences and send
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们应该汇编一本《非预期后果国际期刊》，并把它

sentences.en: them to lawmakers all over the planet.
sentences.zh: 寄给全球的立法者。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Because that's what this is.
sentences.zh: 因为事实就是如此。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Now, hoping that the consequences of the next 60 seconds are predictable, Dan, your time
sentences.zh: 现在，希望接下来的60秒后果是可以预测的，丹，你的时间

sentences.en: starts now.
sentences.zh: 现在开始。

sentences.en: We all know traffic, exhaust, and air pollution are harmful, but what about traffic noise?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道交通、尾气和空气污染是有害的，但交通噪音呢？

sentences.en: Is it a health hazard or just an annoyance?
sentences.zh: 它是健康危害还是仅仅是一种烦恼？

sentences.en: A team of British researchers looked at data on 8.6 million people in neighborhoods across
sentences.zh: 一个英国研究小组查看了伦敦各地社区860万人的数据，

sentences.en: London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦。

sentences.en: Then they analyzed their exposure to daytime and nighttime traffic noise and compared that
sentences.zh: 然后他们分析了这些人白天和夜间接触交通噪音的情况，并将其与

sentences.en: to a range of health data.
sentences.zh: 一系列健康数据进行了比较。

sentences.en: What they found, even after controlling for race, sex, air pollution levels, socioeconomic
sentences.zh: 他们发现，即使在控制了种族、性别、空气污染水平、社会经济

sentences.en: status, and other factors, was sobering.
sentences.zh: 地位和其他因素后，结果依然令人清醒。

sentences.en: Adults exposed to long-term daytime road traffic noise had lower life expectancies and were more
sentences.zh: 长期暴露在白天道路交通噪音中的成年人预期寿命更短，并且比生活在更安静地区的人

sentences.en: likely to be admitted to the hospital for strokes than people living in quieter areas.
sentences.zh: 更容易因中风而住院。

sentences.en: This was especially true for elderly residents.
sentences.zh: 对于老年居民来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: Now, the researchers found only a correlation and the effect wasn't huge, but other evidence
sentences.zh: 现在，研究人员只发现了相关性，而且影响并不巨大，但其他证据

sentences.en: has shown that constantly being around loud traffic triggers stress hormones, which are
sentences.zh: 表明，长期处于嘈杂的交通环境中会触发压力荷尔蒙，这与

sentences.en: linked to hypertension and occasionally death.
sentences.zh: 高血压甚至偶尔的死亡有关。

sentences.en: Bottom line, that racket you hear in certain areas of big cities, honking, idling, revving, may
sentences.zh: 底线是，你在大城市某些地区听到的那种喧嚣，鸣笛、怠速、轰鸣，可能

sentences.en: be harming people who aren't even in the cars.
sentences.zh: 正在伤害那些甚至不在车里的人。

sentences.en: So interesting, Dan.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了，丹。

sentences.en: Is it possible that this is being driven just by the fact that you have more noise pollution
sentences.zh: 有没有可能这仅仅是因为城市地区有更多的噪音污染，

sentences.en: in urban areas and there may be other factors in urban areas that increase the mortality rate?
sentences.zh: 而城市地区可能还有其他因素增加了死亡率？

sentences.en: Well, possibly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有可能。

sentences.en: But they actually did a good job of controlling for a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上在控制这些因素方面做得很好。

sentences.en: They divided up the city into census tracts and actually compared census tracts to each
sentences.zh: 他们把城市划分成人口普查区，并实际上将人口普查区进行了

sentences.en: other.
sentences.zh: 相互比较。

sentences.en: And the census tracts that had more noise had worse health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 噪音更多的人口普查区健康状况更差。

sentences.en: Again, even after you control for the things we know drive health outcomes, especially socioeconomic
sentences.zh: 再次强调，即使在你控制了我们已知会影响健康结果的因素，特别是社会经济

sentences.en: status.
sentences.zh: 地位之后。

sentences.en: So there was something about noise that seemed to be producing these ill effects.
sentences.zh: 所以噪音中似乎确实存在某种导致这些不良影响的东西。

sentences.en: So let me turn it over to you for your 60 seconds.
sentences.zh: 那么让我把时间交给你，进行你的60秒。

sentences.en: But I'd like you, in light of this study, to do it very quietly.
sentences.zh: 但我希望你鉴于这项研究，能非常安静地进行。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we've heard that noise can be bad for you, but can making noise also save your life?
sentences.zh: 所以我们听说噪音对你有害，但制造噪音也能救你的命吗？

sentences.en: James Habiyarimana and William Jack at Georgetown University analyzed two interventions in Kenya
sentences.zh: 乔治城大学的詹姆斯·哈比亚里马纳和威廉·杰克分析了肯尼亚的两项干预措施，

sentences.en: to improve traffic safety.
sentences.zh: 以改善交通安全。

sentences.en: The government passed a set of laws to limit unsafe driving among minibus drivers.
sentences.zh: 政府通过了一系列法律来限制小巴司机的危险驾驶行为。

sentences.en: These are vans that hold a dozen passengers.
sentences.zh: 这些是载有十几名乘客的面包车。

sentences.en: They are private versions of public transit.
sentences.zh: 它们是公共交通的私人版本。

sentences.en: The laws turned out to have very little effect on road safety.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些法律对道路安全几乎没有影响。

sentences.en: What worked was a second initiative where passengers on the minibuses were encouraged to, quote,
sentences.zh: 有效的是第二项倡议，即鼓励小巴上的乘客，引用的话说，

sentences.en: heckle and chide drivers for unsafe driving.
sentences.zh: 对司机的危险驾驶行为进行“质问和责备”。

sentences.en: Stickers on the buses said, don't just sit there, stand up, speak up.
sentences.zh: 公交车上的贴纸写着：不要只是坐着，站起来，说出来。

sentences.en: When consumers were encouraged to make some noise, driver behavior improved radically and
sentences.zh: 当消费者被鼓励制造一些噪音时，司机的行为得到了根本性的改善，

sentences.en: minibus crashes dropped by at least 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 小巴事故减少了至少50%。

sentences.en: Now, we don't know what exactly drove this.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们不知道究竟是什么推动了这一点。

sentences.en: Maybe people spoke up.
sentences.zh: 也许人们真的说了出来。

sentences.en: Maybe the driver was afraid people would speak up.
sentences.zh: 也许司机害怕人们会说出来。

sentences.en: But whatever it was, it worked.
sentences.zh: 但无论是什么，它奏效了。

sentences.en: That is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 这太非凡了。

sentences.en: And I also think that we should rename this show Heckle and Chide.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为我们应该把这个节目改名为《质问与责备》。

sentences.en: You can be Heckle.
sentences.zh: 你可以是“质问”。

sentences.en: I can be Chide.
sentences.zh: 我可以是“责备”。

sentences.en: But I actually think a lot of this shows power to the people.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上认为这在很大程度上展示了人民的力量。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can I be Dr. Heckle and can you be Mr. Chide?
sentences.zh: 我可以是质问博士，而你可以是责备先生吗？

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So there you have it.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是这样。

sentences.en: Building new roads can lead to more congestion and banning people from driving can increase
sentences.zh: 修建新道路可能导致更多的拥堵，而禁止人们开车可能会增加

sentences.en: pollution.
sentences.zh: 污染。

sentences.en: Traffic noise is not just unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 交通噪音不仅仅是不愉快。

sentences.en: It can have health consequences.
sentences.zh: 它可能会带来健康后果。

sentences.en: Finally, before you pass a new law to solve a problem, try to empower the people with
sentences.zh: 最后，在你通过新法律解决问题之前，试着赋予那些

sentences.en: the problem to fix it themselves.
sentences.zh: 面临问题的人权力，让他们自己去解决。

sentences.en: Dan, thanks for joining me on Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 丹，感谢你参加我的《秒表科学》节目。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: I have to get back in my car now.
sentences.zh: 我现在得回到我的车里了。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain Podcast is produced by Cara McGurk-Allison, Maggie Penman, and Max Nestrack.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》播客由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森、玛吉·彭曼和马克斯·内斯特拉克制作。

sentences.en: You can find us on Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram, and listen to my stories on your local
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook、Twitter和Instagram上找到我们，并在你当地的

sentences.en: public radio station.
sentences.zh: 公共广播电台收听我的故事。

sentences.en: If you like this episode, please leave us a review on iTunes.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这一集，请在iTunes上给我们留下评论。

sentences.en: It'll help other people find the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这将帮助其他人找到这个播客。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，这是NPR。
